data.headline: Qualcomm rallies as investors focus on diversification strategy
data.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) extended its premarket gains after beating fourth-quarter expectations and issuing a positive outlook for the current quarter. The chipmaker also approved a $15 billion stock buyback. Moor Insights & Strategy Founder, CEO, and Chief Analyst Patrick Moorhead, breaks down what the Qualcomm rally means for investors with Brad Smith and Seana Smith. Moorhead shares that investors should focus on Qualcomm’s diversification strategy. “Five years ago, Qualcomm only stood for smartphones,” Moorhead said. “While smartphones are a very large percentage of their revenues, they've diversified into a gigantic automotive business with a $45 billion backlog.” To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Morning Brief here. This post was written by Cindy Mizaku.

data.headline: Qualcomm Stock Rallies After Smartphone Demand Fuels Strong Sales
data.summary: Qualcomm reported a jump in quarterly revenue and a near-doubling in profit, amid stronger appetite for the smartphones and other electronics in which its chips feature. In addition to beating sales estimates for last quarter, Qualcomm's revenue forecast of $10.5 billion to $11.3 billion for this quarter topped expectations.

data.headline: Qualcomm advances on smartphone market revival, Chinese handset launches
data.summary: The company, the biggest supplier of smartphone chips, will add around $8 billion to its market value, if the gains hold.  It forecast both first-quarter sales and adjusted profit above market estimates on Wednesday, signaling the smartphone market was picking up after a tough 2023 as consumers upgrade devices for AI apps such as chatbots and image generators.  Demand has been especially positive in major market China, from which Qualcomm gets nearly half its revenue, thanks to new smartphone launches by brands such as Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo.
